name: Almost All Divisors
description: We guessed some integer number $$$x$$$. You are given a list of almost all its divisors. Almost all means that there are all divisors except $$$1$$$ and $$$x$$$ in the list. Your task is to find the minimum possible integer $$$x$$$ that can be the guessed number, or say that the input data is contradictory and it is impossible to find such number. You have to answer $$$t$$$ independent queries.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 25$$$) — the number of queries. Then $$$t$$$ queries follow. The first line of the query contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 300$$$) — the number of divisors in the list. The second line of the query contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$d_1, d_2, \dots, d_n$$$ ($$$2 \le d_i \le 10^6$$$), where $$$d_i$$$ is the $$$i$$$-th divisor of the guessed number. It is guaranteed that all values $$$d_i$$$ are distinct .
output_specification: For each query print the answer to it. If the input data in the query is contradictory and it is impossible to find such number $$$x$$$ that the given list of divisors is the list of almost all its divisors, print -1 . Otherwise print the minimum possible $$$x$$$.
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1165D — Almost All Divisors [242. Sieve, Prime Factorization and Divisors]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every composite integer $X$ has at least one prime factor $\le \sqrt{X}$. Precomputing the Smallest Prime Factor (SPF) for all numbers up to $M$ via a linear sieve allows any $X \le M$ to be completely prime-factorized in $O(\log X)$ steps.
